model.name: Campaign
model.purpose: Represent a governed, coordinated set of activities directed at defined audiences, subjects or environments to produce intended outcomes over a bounded period without absorbing the masters it coordinates.
model.scope_statement: Owns campaign identity and lineage, mandate and problem context, campaign strategy and logic model, objectives, audience and segment definitions, phases and waves, campaign-scoped assignments and variants, message and channel intent, lifecycle, metric definitions and campaign aggregation views, attribution and evaluation assertions, projections, access and retention. Party, project, program, initiative, activity, content, channel, budget, contract, order, payment, event, incident, observation, dataset, policy and generic audit masters remain external.
in_scope: Campaign identity, class, mandate, owner, problem baseline, scope, objectives, outcome logic, audiences, segments, safeguards and exclusions
Phases, waves, activities, experiments, messages, offers, assets, channels, schedules, roles, assignments, budgets and resource references, risks and controls
Authorization, release, launch, pause, resume, change, termination, observations, metrics, evaluation, attribution, learning, interoperability, access, retention and agent operations
out_of_scope: Party, project, program, initiative, activity, content, channel, account, budget, contract, order, payment, event, incident, observation, dataset, policy or audit-log master lifecycle
Inferring individual audience membership, delivery, exposure, engagement, conversion, behavior change, impact or causation without a source-qualified assertion and method

Implementing advertising exchanges, social networks, campaign schedulers, content management, payments, analytics engines or universal legal compliance and claiming lossless cross-platform equivalence

boundary_notes.distinction: A campaign may be governed as a project or participate in a program, but this root owns audience or target-directed strategy, waves, messages and campaign measurement, not generic delivery governance.
The campaign owns versioned target definitions and eligibility rules; external person, organization, group and membership assertions keep their identity, authority and lifecycle.
Campaign-scoped assignments and release bindings are owned here, while executable activities, messages, assets, channels, placements and accounts remain external masters.
The campaign defines metric use and aggregation and records campaign-specific evaluation; source observations, datasets and external decisions keep independent provenance.
STIX and Google Ads are sector or platform projections. Neither narrows the vendor-neutral root to malicious activity or paid advertising.

sources.title: Activity Vocabulary

sources.title: Activity Streams 2.0
sources.relevance: Defines JSON-LD serialization and collection and activity processing for interoperable campaign projections.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Defines entity, activity, agent, responsibility, generation, derivation, revision and attribution provenance.

sources.title: The RDF Data Cube Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines observations, measures, dimensions, attributes, slices, datasets and data-structure definitions for metric observations.

sources.title: ISO 21502:2020 Project, programme and portfolio management - Guidance on project management
sources.relevance: Provides the project-management boundary and practices used to distinguish a campaign coordination aggregate from a project master.

sources.title: Evaluate complex campaigns
sources.relevance: Defines campaign logic models across inputs, activities, outputs, outcomes and impacts and warns that impact attribution is difficult.

sources.title: Applying communication for health: planning guide
sources.relevance: Defines a six-step communication-intervention cycle: understand, plan, develop, test, implement, evaluate and learn.

sources.title: Module 1: Communication Planning
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.relevance: Identifies goals, audience, messages, methods or tactics, timeline, responsibility, budget and evaluation as communication-plan elements.

sources.title: Audience
sources.relevance: Defines intended audience, audience type and geographic area for cross-sector discovery projections.

sources.title: Action
sources.relevance: Defines action status, agent, object, participant, instrument, target, result, place and start and end times.

sources.title: Google Ads API Campaign resource
sources.relevance: Provides one explicitly platform-scoped campaign projection covering status, channel type, audience settings, budgets, bidding, experiments and serving state.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines seconds and explicit-offset timestamps for campaign events, observations and knowledge time.

functions.name: Register and authorize campaign
functions.description: Establish campaign identity, boundary, mandate, owner and governing profile.
preconditions: identity, duplicate, mandate, scope, safety and privacy validate
effects: a governed root exists without launching activity

functions.name: Define strategy, objectives and logic model
functions.description: Record intended change, measurable objectives and testable causal assumptions.
preconditions: scope, baseline, outcome definitions, indicators, assumptions and authority validate
effects: planning claims become versioned and falsifiable

functions.name: Define audiences, eligibility and safeguards
functions.description: Create versioned segment rules, exclusions, consent or authority and protections.
preconditions: purpose, criteria, data authority, suppression, risk and bias validate
effects: targeting intent is bounded without copying person masters

functions.name: Plan waves, activities, messages and channels
functions.description: Coordinate campaign-scoped work and external delivery objects.
preconditions: dependencies, schedule, roles, approvals, accessibility and capacity validate
effects: an executable plan exists without asserting delivery

functions.name: Approve and release campaign material
functions.description: Bind approved message, offer, asset and placement versions to a campaign release.
preconditions: claim, content, rights, audience, channel, expiry and approval validate
effects: specific material becomes eligible for controlled delivery

functions.name: Launch, pause, resume or terminate
functions.description: Append an authorized operating-state event across declared scope.
preconditions: expected revision, gate, authority, risk, time and downstream controls validate
effects: operating state changes without rewriting prior releases

functions.name: Record delivery and result observations
functions.description: Attach source-qualified activity and metric observations at defined levels.
preconditions: source, period, unit, denominator, segment, deduplication, quality and freshness validate
effects: delivery, reach, exposure, engagement, conversion, outcome and impact remain distinguishable

functions.name: Evaluate and attribute results
functions.description: Apply a declared evaluation and attribution method and record bounded conclusions.
preconditions: method version, counterfactual, window, assumptions, confounders and uncertainty validate
effects: decisions can cite evidence without claiming unsupported causation

functions.name: Revise, close and capture learning

preconditions: authority, expected head, impact, unresolved risks, disposition and applicability validate
effects: current plan changes while released history and limits remain visible

functions.name: Project, validate, retain and audit

preconditions: identity, version, mapping loss, access, legal hold, minimum tombstone and post-checks validate
effects: campaign data remains interoperable and accountable under policy

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint stable IDs for campaign roots, releases, waves, assignments, events and campaign-scoped assertions. Preserve authoritative external party, project, activity, content, channel, budget, contract, event and dataset identities; never use campaign name or dates as identity.
registry_links: Dimension-local campaign, objective, audience, channel, metric and policy registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize a campaign by authoritative source plus campaign identifier and current lineage head, not by name, objective, audience, period, channel or digest.
Keep plan, forecast, target, released assignment, observed result and analyst interpretation as different assertion classes with source and time.
patch_rules: Extensions declare campaign profile, target finding, semantics, authority, lifecycle, privacy, safety, measurement and interoperability impact.
Released plans and observations are immutable. Corrections, strategy changes, segment changes and profile upgrades create successors with preserved provenance.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, authority, objectives, audience, activity, lifecycle, measurement and provenance remain intact.
STIX, ActivityStreams, Schema.org, Data Cube and platform mappings pin versions and declare omissions, semantic conflicts and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system campaign identifier qualified by source and campaign class.
Governed globally resolvable campaign IRI under a controlled namespace.
Dimension UUID when no authoritative or governed global identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate planned, release, event, effective, observation, ingestion and knowledge times and preserve source precision.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {campaign-id}--{phase-or-wave-id-or-root}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use campaign name, date, timestamp or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, campaign and release binding, source and profile versions, authority, event and knowledge times, audience and access marking and provenance.

policies: Plan, target, forecast, release, delivery, reach, exposure, engagement, conversion, outcome, impact and causal attribution are separate attributable assertions.
Campaign ownership does not transfer ownership of people, audiences, projects, content, channels, budgets, contracts, events, observations, policy or audit masters.
Audience criteria, suppression, consent or authority, vulnerable-group safeguards and adverse-effect monitoring are versioned and purpose-bound.

Agents may validate and project allowlisted data, but audience expansion, release, launch, spending, political or health targeting, protected disclosure and destructive disposition require delegated authority and policy controls.

access.default_rule: Deny person-level audience data, segment membership, suppression lists, contact endpoints, unpublished strategy, security tactics, political or health targeting and raw cross-channel linkage; disclose purpose-bound minimum aggregates and approved material.
exceptions: Participant-self, campaign operator, safety response, auditor, regulator or court access cites authority and remains minimum-necessary, time-limited and separately logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, campaign, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, release or affected fields, source revision and outcome without copying protected audience data unnecessarily.

coverage.claim: Single-provider Codex result covering a cross-sector Campaign coordination aggregate across 6 bundles, 12 layers, 24 findings, 72 questions, 24 artifacts and 10 functions grounded in 13 pinned sources, spanning mandate and problem context, strategy and logic model, audiences and safeguards, waves, messages, channels, roles, resources, risk, lifecycle, source-qualified measurement, bounded attribution, interoperability, access and governed disposition. Coverage here is structural, not verified: the provider's all-sixteen-dimensions-covered checklist is downgraded to partial because q02 and q03 are template-identical across every finding, all 24 artifacts share one media_or_form and identity template, no approved relation rows exist, and neither live source resolution nor independent second-provider review was performed. No claim of universal, cross-sector or cross-jurisdictional completeness is made.

checklist.notes: Campaign root, release, wave, assignment, event and assertion identities are distinct.
Cross-sector campaign definition and project, program, initiative, operation and event boundaries are explicit.
Mandate, objectives, audiences, strategy, work, content, channel, lifecycle and metrics are first-class.
Delivery and result observations retain source, level, period, denominator, quality and uncertainty.
Register, define, plan, release, transition, observe, evaluate, revise, project and audit are governed.
Party, project, activity, content, channel, budget, contract, event, dataset, policy and audit masters remain external.
Draft, review, authorization, release, launch, pause, resume, change, termination and closure preserve history.
Objectives, audiences, waves, activities, assets, channels, resources, metrics and external masters use typed links.
Planned, release, event, effective, observation, ingestion and knowledge times remain distinct.
Audience geography, operating context, origin, target and activity location are source-qualified.
Plans, releases, assignments, events, observations, evaluations and projections preserve responsible-agent provenance.
Sponsor, strategist, audience, safety, content, channel, delivery, evaluation, privacy and records duties are separated.
Identity, mandate, audience, lifecycle, schedule, deduplication, denominator, method and stale-head checks are explicit.
Purpose-bound views, audience protection, suppression and deny-by-default person-level linkage are explicit.
Delivery stop, live-state termination, working-copy deletion, retained lineage, legal hold and tombstones are distinguished.
STIX, ActivityStreams, Schema.org, Data Cube and platform projections are versioned and loss-aware.

known_omissions: No successful independent Claude or Grok result was available; later cross-sector, political, public-health, marketing, fundraising, advocacy, security and legal review is required before canonical promotion.
No approved relation rows were supplied; the registry parent link to Project and proposed party, activity, content, channel, budget, event, observation, policy and audit links remain holds.
Sector profiles need their own legal controls, vocabularies, delivery semantics, safety constraints, measurement conventions and interoperability tests.
Google Ads v23 is only one commercial platform mapping and must never define vendor-neutral campaign semantics.
conflicts: Campaign may denote a coordination plan, a set of observed adversarial behaviors or a platform advertising container; profiles must declare which assertions are planned, controlled or inferred.
Audience targeting, personalization, measurement, cross-channel identity resolution, privacy, fairness and safety objectives can conflict.
Platform-attributed conversions, observational outcomes and causal impact estimates can disagree while each remains valid under its source method.
regional_assumptions: Political communication, advertising, fundraising, health claims, consent, profiling, suppression, record retention and disclosure depend on jurisdiction and sector.
WHO and CDC guidance informs communication and public-health profiles but does not define all campaign types.
STIX defines adversarial campaigns and Google Ads defines one advertising platform; both are explicit profiles rather than universal masters.
adversarial_checks: Reject a campaign whose identity, mandate, boundary, current release, objective or owner cannot be resolved.
Reject delivery, reach, exposure, engagement, conversion, outcome, impact or causation inferred from a neighboring metric without source and method.
Reject silent audience, objective, message, activity, schedule, budget, status, metric or attribution mutation and any history rewrite.
Reject person-level targeting, suppression removal or cross-channel linkage without purpose, authority, safeguards, access control and audit.

Reject an agent operation that expands audience, releases content, launches delivery, commits spend, makes protected political or health targeting changes or destroys held evidence without delegated authority.
